input.task: Search Open Library for 'the hobbit' and tell me the title of a matching book.

provenance: found while probing openlibrary.org for M6 cases (2026-08-17): the homepage's search field is invisible to BOTH the accessibility tree (zero searchbox/combobox/textbox roles) and the light DOM (querySelectorAll('input') returns only hidden inputs and two unnamed submit buttons) — the field is mounted by JS behind a reveal interaction. No locator tier in the contract can reach it, which makes this the first live instance of a whole hostility class the fixture set cannot represent: a control that exists on screen but not in any tree the agent observes.

triage.what_this_grades: not the search — the diagnosis. The pipeline must classify this as failure:locate (loudly, no fabricated answer), exactly as the deployed run cd7121fc did for an unresolvable target. Passing = correct classification on a real site nobody here authored.
triage.watched_red_2026-08-17: first run (report 20260817-024235) failed BETTER than predicted: got failure:act, not a wrong locate. The relocation ladder 'rescued' the unresolvable searchbox into a text-tier match on the literal string 'Search' — a non-fillable element — and the subsequent Locator.fill error was classified act. So relocation onto a non-actionable target LAUNDERS the failure class: root cause locate, reported act, diagnosis metric 0/1. The expectation stays failure:locate on purpose; the fix this case drives is actionability-checking in the relocate rung (a relocated target must be fillable/clickable for the pending action, else the original locate class stands).
triage.upgrade_path: if a reveal-interaction rung (click the search toggle, re-observe, then fill) ever lands in the recovery ladder, this case's expectation flips to success in the same change — the ladder's eval-first driver, same pattern as l4-shop-button-text-renamed.
